The test image shows a cross-section of a corn stalk with:
- Heavy dark black discoloration/necrosis on the outer stalk ring
- White/cream disintegrated pith interior (wet-looking)
- Some yellow-orange coloring in center
- Completely rotted internal tissue

This is clearly a **stalk rot**. Top candidates: Charcoal_stalk_rot, Diplodia_stalk_rot, Anthracnose_stalk_rot, Fusarium stalk rot. Let me view reference images.
The Physoderma_stalk_rot reference image is very promising - it shows the same dark outer ring with lighter interior cross-section. Let me compare with a couple more candidates.

Now I have enough information to make my assessment.

**Analysis summary:**

**Test image features:**
- Cross-section of a corn stalk (two cross-sections visible)
- Very dark/black necrotic outer ring
- White/cream wet-looking rotted pith interior
- Some yellowish material in center
- Slimy/wet appearance

**Reference comparison:**
- **Charcoal stalk rot**: Gray/tan shredded pith, not a stark black ring — doesn't match
- **Diplodia stalk rot**: Brown exterior/tan pith disintegration, no stark black ring — doesn't match
- **Anthracnose stalk rot**: Black external lesions, brown/shredded interior — partial match but pith is shredded/dry, not white/wet
- **Bacterial stalk rot**: Wet collapse but reference shows field wilting, not this cross-section pattern
- **Fusarium**: Pink/salmon pith — doesn't match
- **Physoderma stalk rot**: Reference clearly shows a broken stalk cross-section with a very dark/black outer ring and cream/white lighter interior — **best match**

The Physoderma stalk rot reference images (especially lower panels) show exactly this pattern: dark blackened outer ring on the stalk cross-section with lighter pith interior — closely matching the test image.
